title: publishing the machine install never deletes a file devbin stopped shipping, so every estate keeps receiving it as devbin-owned
body:
FOUND 2026-09-23 while 0113's consumer page for upgrade was checked against the code. Reproduced by the page audit in a scratch source and install (`t_pub2.sh`), and read by cc at 142763d.

WHAT HAPPENS. When devbin's source stops shipping a file under lib/, the machine install keeps it, and every estate seeded or upgraded from the install then receives it, recorded in that estate's manifest as devbin-owned.

WHY:
- publish_install in lib/install copies each file in `vendored_paths <source>` into the install and rewrites the manifest from the same list. Nothing deletes a file that is in the install but no longer in the source. Its own comment calls what follows "a full replace", and it is not one. The manifest drops the file while the disk keeps it.
- An estate then vendors FROM the install, and `vendored_paths <install>` enumerates the install's lib/ with `find`, so the orphan is back on the list.
- A project upgrade does retire a file its source stopped shipping, unless it was edited. That removal never fires, because the file never stops being shipped from the install the estates read.

WHY IT MATTERS. Removing a file from devbin's lib/ is the one change the seam cannot deliver. The file lingers in every estate, and a stale `lib/cmd/<name>` handler, or a sourced module that still defines a function, is behaviour, not clutter. devbin has no file removed under lib/ in flight today, so nothing is exposed yet; the first deletion will be.

THE FIX belongs in publish_install: remove what the install holds under bin/.devbin/lib/ that the source no longer ships, and say so in the report.

## Resolution

Fixed at c585f3d, one commit with 0127, 0129 and 0140. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. Publish removes what the machine install holds under bin/.devbin/lib/ and the source no longer ships, prunes the directories that leaves empty, and names each removal. upgrade.md's publish-upgrade paragraph says so. One removal, remove_unshipped in lib/install, serves publish and a project's install --force (0129). It removes on the answer the vendored-set reads give, and those read their status (0127). And it keeps a file devbin renamed only in case, on a disk that folds case (0140).
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. At 0113's landing, every arm but three was red for the reason it names. V1-V10, W1-W5 and Y1-Y9 were killed, each by the arm aimed at it. Y3 was killed on a case-sensitive image, and Y7a is an exercise. The commit message lists them.
- REVIEW. vc approved v2 after driving a case-only rename through publish, install --force and upgrade, intact and edited. The full suite on the landing tree then failed two helpers.bats scans: a raw shasum in one of this commit's tests, and bare `mv --` lines in keep_case_twin, which can block on a terminal prompt. v3 fixed both, and vc approved its interdiff.
- THE SUITE. On 0ec1fbf plus v3: 1..1694, 1694 ok, 0 not ok, 5 expected skips, rc 0. It landed through the gate, and the commit holds the build's bytes on all 11 paths. vc's own full suite before the landing, on 6c9fbc6 plus v3final in vc's clone, read the same: 1..1694, 1694 ok, 0 not ok, 5 expected skips, rc 0, 09:02:21Z to 09:33:51Z.
